evidence_excerpt: 1. Start with initialization setting managementFee = 200. 2. Call setManagementFee(200) which is allowed because 200 <= maxManagementFee. 3. Later, governance might call setMaxManagementFee(100) because 100 <= MANAGEMENT_FEE_HARD_CAP. 4. Stored state becomes managementFee = 200 > maxManagementFee = 100, so the "always" invariant breaks, which was the following: managementFee <= maxManagementFee (always).

The test confirms an MV-SCAN hit. It is a griefing bug in the Spartan DAO, isn't currently in the ground truth list, and is identical to the pattern that M-04 points out for SynthVault at a different contract. I show that the victim deposits LP once, waits 10 days, and victim calls harvest(). The result is 50,000 SPARTA. The attack run: same setup. Before victim harvests, attacker calls to connect to the dao, then the victim harvests. The result is a griefing of the victim, from 50,000 SPARTA to 2 SPARTA. Attacker earns 0 SPARTA. This is a pay-to-grief scheme that allows an attacker to sacrifice some LP to almost completely nuke the victim's rewards with no direct profit involvement.

Genuinely new governance bug introducing an admin self-grief. I classify this as zero-day because it goes against intended behavior, specified by some of the findings (e.g. "Bad actor on governance side cannot permanently lock protocol, pools, etc."). Proof of correctness: Take any state with params.governanceDelay <= MAX_GOVERNANCE_DELAY. An admin calls setPendingParams(newParams) with newParams.governanceDelay > MAX_GOVERNANCE_DELAY, which passes because the require checks the old governanceDelay. After the delay, commitParams is called, setting params = pendingParams, so params.governanceDelay > MAX_GOVERNANCE_DELAY holds, and from then on every call to setPendingParams reverts at require(params.governanceDelay <= MAX_GOVERNANCE_DELAY). Symmetric to [H-04] pattern, here is the zero-day: syncUSDVPrice() is the exact same flaw from H-04, where we initialize local _totalLiquidityWeight = 0, skips pairs when timeElapsed < updatePeriod, and still writes totalLiquidityWeight[USDV] = _totalLiquidityWeight at the end. At a second call, all pairs have timeElapsed = 0 so all are skipped, which leads to _totalLiquidityWeight staying 0 and leads to the storage weight equaling 0. A sketch for an exploit: 1. Wait until >= 1 USDV pair is eligible for update. 2. Call syncUSDVPrice() once which updates lastMeasurement for updated pairs. 3. Call syncUSDVPrice() again immediately within the same block. 4. Now totalLiquidityWeight[USDV] == 0 until someone syncs after updatePeriod.
